script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Forty-year-old JAMES, an IT consultant, sits on a worn-out couch, staring at the television with a vacant look in his eyes. He swallows a mouthful of coffee and rubs his forehead.

JAMES
(murmuring to himself)
Another day, another dollar.

His wife, EMMA, walks in, wearing a business suit and carrying a briefcase. She sits next to him, placing her hand on his shoulder.

EMMA
(softly)
James, you've been saying that for weeks now. Maybe it's time for a change.

INT. JAMES' HOME OFFICE - LATER

James sits at his desk, surrounded by computer screens, staring blankly at the code in front of him. He sighs and leans back in his chair, looking defeated.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James sits across from his friend, MIKE, a painter. They sip their coffees in silence, each lost in thought.

MIKE
(looking up from his cup)
You know, you've been talking about leaving the IT world for ages. What's stopping you?

James looks away, unsure of what to say.

JAMES
I don't know. Fear, I guess. Fear of the unknown.

INT. ART GALLERY - DAY

James wanders through the gallery, taking in the various pieces of art. He feels drawn to a particular painting – a vibrant landscape with bold colors.

INT. JAMES' HOME OFFICE - NIGHT

James sits at his desk, staring at the blank screen in front of him. He can't bring himself to write another line of code. He takes a deep breath and makes a decision.

INT. ART SUPPLY STORE - DAY

James enters the store, looking around in awe at the various art supplies. He purchases a set of paints, brushes, and a canvas.

INT. JAMES' HOME STUDIO - DAY

James sets up his makeshift studio in a spare room. He spends hours each day learning the basics of painting, experimenting with colors and techniques.

INT. ART CLASS - DAY

James attends his first art class, surrounded by students of all ages. He feels out of place but determined. The instructor, ALEX, notices his hesitation and approaches him.

ALEX
(smiling)
You look unsure. What brings you here?

JAMES
I've decided to make a change. I want to learn how to paint.

Alex nods, offering him a warm smile.

ALEX
Well, welcome to the world of art, James. It's never too late to start.

INT. JAMES' HOME STUDIO - DAY

Months later, James stands back and admires his latest painting. He's proud of his progress, but he knows there's still a long way to go.

INT. ART GALLERY - NIGHT

James attends an opening night reception for a local art exhibit. He nervously sets up his painting among the others. Guests mill about, admiring the artwork.

A woman, ISABELLA, approaches James' painting, studying it intently. She turns to him, a look of admiration in her eyes.

ISABELLA
This is beautiful. Where did you learn to paint like this?

James beams with pride.

JAMES
Thank you. I'm still learning, but I'm determined to make it my career.

Isabella smiles, exchanging contact information with James.

INT. JAMES' HOME STUDIO - DAY

James spends hours each day perfecting his craft, working tirelessly to create masterpieces. He receives a call from Isabella, offering him an opportunity to showcase his work in a prestigious gallery.

INT. PRESTIGIOUS GALLERY - NIGHT

James stands in the gallery, surrounded by fellow artists and admirers, taking in the scene before him. He feels a sense of accomplishment and pride.

FADE OUT.

THE END
